questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn to catch your exit. If you miss your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes on a multilane highway?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no one is there.

questions.question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
Where there is a red light.
When a traffic officer orders you to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: What should you check before starting your vehicle?

options.text: Only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
All passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: All passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting your vehicle, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing lights. Pull over to the right side of the road. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic on green must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic on green must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way and must wait for oncoming traffic to pass.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red warning lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Copy what other drivers are doing instead of following the guard.
Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow the regular rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from a crossing guard or traffic officer. Slow down and be extra careful in school zones.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a traffic crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to hours between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most important thing you can do to protect yourself from death or injury while driving.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: A minor traffic safety problem.
A serious traffic safety problem.
Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired or drunk is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or using drugs. It puts you and others on the road at risk.

questions.question: Littering:

options.text: Is against the law.
Can cause a traffic accident.
Can result in a $1,000 fine and up to one year in jail.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Littering is illegal. It looks bad and can cause accidents. For example, a lit cigarette thrown from your car can blow into the car behind you and cause damage or injury. If you are found guilty of littering, you may pay up to $1,000 and spend up to one year in jail.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are turning.
Have your parking brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly whenever you drive.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
A stop sign is present.
Red flashing lights and gates are working.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign directs you to stop. Also stop when you see red flashing lights and gates that are working.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, surviving a crash is very unlikely. Driving slower than other traffic is also dangerous because drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction will become one lane ahead.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway:

options.text: Stop and turn around.
Exit at the next exit and turn around there.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit at the next exit and turn around there.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up or turn around on the highway. Go to the next exit and turn around safely.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces how the alcohol affects you.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
Together they can multiply the effects of each other.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: Together they can multiply the effects of each other.
questions.explanation: Drinking alcohol while taking medicine can increase how much each affects you. For example, one drink with cold medicine can affect you as much as several drinks alone.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says something different.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if there were no construction.

questions.explanation: Slow down and follow instructions from signs, flaggers, or police in construction zones. Failing to do so is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way to drive around lowered gates.
Assume no trains are coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be nearby. Obey all warning signs and never go around barriers.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the light turns red.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already inside the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Drive faster to cross before the gate comes down.
Drive around a lowered crossing gate.
Do not worry about how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop at railroad tracks. A train or other vehicle may be using the rails.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Turn the steering wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: You see a driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Keep extra distance from that vehicle.
Understand that the driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Do not drive the same way.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because they are more likely to cause an accident.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for the conditions
Driving too close to other vehicles
All of the above

questions.explanation: Speeding causes many crashes. Not paying attention can lead to collisions. Most rear-end accidents happen because drivers follow too closely.
